body_text:
Let $f : [a, b] \to \mathbb{R}$ be bounded. For each subinterval
$[x_{i-1}, x_i]$ of partition $P$, let $m_i = \inf_{[x_{i-1}, x_i]} f$
and $M_i = \sup_{[x_{i-1}, x_i]} f$.
The *lower Darboux sum* and *upper Darboux sum* are:
$$ L(f, P) = \sum_{i=1}^n m_i (x_i - x_{i-1}) \quad \text{and} \quad U(f, P) = \sum_{i=1}^n M_i (x_i - x_{i-1}). $$

By the Refinement Lemma, if $P' \supseteq P$ is a refinement, then:
$$ L(f, P) \leq L(f, P') \leq U(f, P') \leq U(f, P). $$
Consequently, every lower sum is less than or equal to every upper sum,
regardless of the partitions chosen.
